assumptions: Assumes the app does not clearly explain how these indicators are derived or that such inferences are being made.
uncertainty_note: The flow description confirms display of inferences but not whether explanatory notice is provided.

title: User may lack control over whether sensitive inferred indicators are shown
description: If the wearer cannot configure, suppress, or limit the display of eating-disorder or diabetes risk indicators, they lack meaningful control over this sensitive processing and disclosure to themselves and potentially nearby observers.
assumptions: Assumes the app may not offer preferences to disable or tailor these dashboard indicators.
uncertainty_note: No settings or consent controls are described, so this is a plausible but unconfirmed threat.

title: Displaying inferred sensitive health-risk indicators may raise lawfulness concerns
description: Presenting inferred eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals involves processing potentially special-category health data and possibly automated profiling. Without an appropriate lawful basis and safeguards, this flow may be non-compliant with data protection requirements.
assumptions: Assumes the inferred indicators qualify as sensitive health-related personal data under the applicable regime.
uncertainty_note: This depends on jurisdiction, lawful basis, and safeguards not provided in the prompt.

title: Insufficient user controls over sensitive dashboard inferences may create compliance risk
description: If the wearer cannot access explanations, object to, disable, or otherwise control the display and processing of sensitive inferred condition indicators, the system may fail to support relevant data subject rights and controls.
assumptions: Assumes limited user controls around these inferences.
uncertainty_note: The prompt does not specify whether such controls exist.

title: Full health and location dataset enables strong linkage of records
description: The flow sends analytics data, models, and the full health and location dataset to the cloud provider. The combination of health data with precise location data creates a strong quasi-identifier set that can link records belonging to the same individual across datasets or over time.
assumptions: Assumes the hosted dataset contains per-person records or longitudinal data rather than only fully aggregated anonymous outputs.

title: Hosted health and location data is likely identifiable through quasi-identifiers
description: At the cloud hosting provider, the full health and location dataset is processed and stored. Even if direct identifiers are absent, combinations of health attributes, location traces, and analytics context can make data subjects identifiable.
assumptions: Assumes the dataset is not irreversibly anonymized before transfer.

title: Stored analytics and dataset records can become attributable evidence about individuals
description: Replication and hosting of the full health and location dataset at the cloud provider creates persistent records that may later be used as evidence tying sensitive conditions, movements, or behaviors to specific individuals, reducing plausible deniability.
assumptions: Assumes records are retained in a form that can be associated with individuals directly or indirectly.
uncertainty_note: Non-repudiation is somewhat context-dependent here because the flow description does not explicitly mention signatures, audit trails, or evidentiary use.

title: Cloud-hosted transfer and replication increase detectability of sensitive activity
description: Sending and replicating analytics data and the full health and location dataset to a third-party cloud provider creates additional observation points where the existence of sensitive processing or particular data subjects may be detected through communications or storage operations.
assumptions: Assumes the provider or parties with access to provider infrastructure can observe transfer, replication, or storage events.
uncertainty_note: The exact detectability mechanism is not described, so this is based on the added observability inherent in third-party hosting and replication.

title: Propagation of the full health and location dataset to a third-party cloud may exceed necessity
description: The flow explicitly hosts and replicates analytics data, models, and the full health and location dataset at an external cloud provider. Making the full dataset accessible to an additional external party and replicating it may disclose personal data beyond what is strictly necessary for the analytics function.
assumptions: Assumes not all raw health and location data must be transferred in full to the provider, or that less granular/minimized data could suffice.

title: Third-party cloud hosting exposes sensitive data to an additional predetermined party
description: The cloud hosting provider is a known external entity receiving hosted and replicated copies of analytics data, models, and the full health and location dataset. This increases exposure of sensitive personal data to a predetermined external party.
assumptions: Assumes the provider can access or potentially access hosted content or metadata in the course of service delivery.

title: Data subjects may be unaware that full health and location data is hosted and replicated by a third party
description: The flow indicates that the full health and location dataset is hosted and replicated at a third-party cloud provider. Data subjects may not be aware that their sensitive data is stored and duplicated outside the primary analytics service.
assumptions: Assumes this third-party hosting and replication is not made fully transparent to data subjects.
uncertainty_note: Awareness depends on notices and transparency mechanisms, which are not described.

title: Third-party replication can hinder erasure or correction of hosted sensitive data
description: Once the full health and location dataset is hosted and replicated at the cloud provider, data subjects may have reduced practical ability to ensure correction or deletion propagates across all hosted and replicated copies.
assumptions: Assumes replication creates multiple copies and deletion/rectification workflows across provider-managed storage are not fully controllable by data subjects.
uncertainty_note: The flow description mentions replication but does not specify whether robust deletion and rectification mechanisms exist.

title: Transferring the full health and location dataset to cloud hosting may violate data minimization
description: The flow states that the full health and location dataset, along with analytics data and models, is hosted and replicated at the cloud provider. Processing and sharing the full dataset with an external party may exceed what is necessary for the stated analytics purpose, creating a data minimization compliance risk.
assumptions: Assumes a reduced, aggregated, or less granular dataset could satisfy the hosting or analytics need.

title: Replication at the cloud provider creates storage limitation compliance risk
description: Because the dataset is hosted and replicated at the cloud provider, multiple copies of sensitive health and location data may persist longer than necessary, increasing the risk of violating storage limitation obligations.
assumptions: Assumes retention periods for hosted and replicated copies are not tightly bounded and enforced.
uncertainty_note: The flow description does not specify retention periods, so this is a risk inference from replication rather than a confirmed violation.
